compilation_result.label: PR #4193: multi-AZ NAT topology + orders-db upsize

assumptions.basis: one-third of the combined 40,000 GB/month assumption for this 3-gateway group, modelled from the orders-api workload's current outbound traffic profile

warnings: Data processing volume is a modelled assumption, not a measured value — this NAT gateway does not exist yet. If actual traffic differs from the orders-api profile used for this estimate, the real cost will differ proportionally.

Instance class change db.r5.large -> db.r5.2xlarge; no evidence of a corresponding utilization finding or discovery recommendation prompted this change — it is not associated with any open optimize.Recommendation.

assumptions.basis: modelled from the orders-api workload's current outbound traffic profile, applied to a topology that does not exist yet

risks.summary: 3 NAT gateways added, one per AZ, combined $1,898.55/month projected cost, 95% of it a usage-dependent data-processing assumption
risks.detail: This estate already carries an unresolved NAT-waste finding of $12,348.00/month on its existing gateways (no S3 VPC endpoint present — see the NAT elimination optimization scenario). Adding three more gateways in a new topology without first addressing the existing finding, or without evaluating whether a shared/consolidated NAT design or additional VPC endpoints would serve this new topology instead, compounds a cost category this tenant is already actively working to reduce.
risks.remediation: Confirm whether an S3 (and other applicable) gateway VPC endpoint is planned for this new topology before merging, and whether 3 independent gateways are required versus a consolidated design; route through architecture review per this tenant's own cost test suite.

results.name: nat-gateway-requires-review
results.expected: no aws_nat_gateway resources in the change set
results.message: New NAT gateways require architecture review before merge — this estate already carries $12,348.00/month of avoidable NAT data-processing waste from gateways added without a VPC endpoint review.

results.name: workload-monthly-increase-cap
results.expected: <= 10.0% increase against the orders-api workload's current baseline ($18,500.00/mo)
results.message: Production monthly cost increase must not exceed 10% of the affected workload's current baseline without explicit sign-off.

results.name: pricing-coverage-floor
results.message: Full pricing coverage — though note 73% of projected monthly cost is usage-dependent modelling (see confidence: 0.74), a different concern from unpriced coverage.
